x: IPR 1956 was called both the "Economic Constitution of India" and the "Bible of State Capitalism", so option B is correct. Option A wrongly links the "Economic Constitution" label to IPR 1948; the Licence-Permit Raj began with IPR 1956, not 1948; and the 1991 policy was not a "mixed economy charter" (IPR 1948 laid the mixed-economy foundation).

Defence equipment, atomic energy and railway transport formed the public-sector-only list, so B is the wrong pair. Drugs and pharmaceuticals were never reserved for the public sector; they appeared only in the older six-industry compulsory-licensing list and were later delicensed.

The V. Krishnamurthy Committee (1991) set out an early disinvestment approach, so A is correct. The Rangarajan Committee was 1993 (49% in reserved PSUs), the Disinvestment Commission was 1996 (case-by-case sale advice, strategic sales), and PSU autonomy/MoUs in 1984 belong to Arjun Sengupta, not Vijay Kelkar.

The 16th Finance Commission proposed closing 308 inactive State PSUs and privatising DISCOMs, so A is correct. NLMC monetises surplus CPSE land and buildings (combinations are regulated by CCI), CCI appeals are heard by NCLAT (IBBI is the IBC regulator), and BIFR dealt with sick companies under SICA.

Under the IBC framework the NCLT is the adjudicating authority, so B is correct. NCLAT is the appellate tribunal (insolvency professionals are licensed, with IBBI as regulator), IBBI is the regulator rather than an appellate body, and SICA was the old regime replaced by the IBC.

All four are correct: the NITI Aayog Investment Friendliness Index (July 2026) uses 953 indicators across 8 pillars, places Andhra Pradesh among the Frontrunners (score 45-50), and names Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Goa and Odisha as Top Performers.

Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014, Digital India on 1 July 2015, Skill India on 15 July 2015 and Startup India on 16 January 2016, so the order is B, C, D, A. Digital India precedes Skill India by two weeks, which rules out option B.
